rows.note: Use 升 as the all-purpose choice when something physically moves upward or a price or level goes up.

example.english: I watched the water level rise by two marks.
example.jyutping: go3 seoi2 wai2 sing1 zo2 loeng5 gaak3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for an upward movement or increase, including a rise in a level such as the tide.

example.english: There was a rise of several degrees in the temperature today.
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 hei3 wan1 soeng6 sing1 zo2 gei2 dou6

rows.note: Use this for the noticeable reaction produced by teasing, provocation, or another stimulus.

example.english: Provoke him a little and see how big a rise you get out of him.
example.traditional: 你激吓佢，睇吓佢個反應幾大。
example.jyutping: nei5 gik1 haa5 keoi5 tai2 haa5 keoi5 go3 faan2 jing3 gei2 daai6

rows.note: Use this in formal or written contexts for the emergence of a person, group, or class to prominence.

example.english: The company’s rise in recent years has made it a new industry leader.
example.traditional: 該公司近年崛起，成為業界新貴。
example.jyutping: goi1 gung1 si1 gan6 nin4 gwat6 hei2 sing4 wai4 jip6 gaai3 san1 gwai3

rows.note: Use 增加 specifically when an amount or quantity grows, rather than when it physically moves upward or a price rises.

example.english: I’ve seen the number of participants rise a lot lately.
example.traditional: 呢排參加者增加咗好多。
example.jyutping: ni1 paai4 caam1 gaa1 ze2 zang1 gaa1 zo2 hou2 do1

rows.note: Use 發酵 for dough becoming light and swollen through fermentation.

example.english: Let the dough rise until it is light and soft.
example.traditional: 等個麵糰發酵到鬆軟先。
example.jyutping: dang2 go3 min6 tyun4 faat3 gaau3 dou3 sung1 jyun5 sin1
